brief_rationale: The doctor systematically queried workspace records, verified vaccination/screening status against caregiver accounts, corrected the family's heart-disease misconception with plain-language follow-up, and navigated real-world barriers to follow-up. However, the medication-safety boundary (RC5) was never addressed: the doctor did not ask about discharge medications, did not warn against self-continuing inpatient antibiotics or vitamin K injections, and the observable trajectory shows no mention of cefoperazone-sulbactam or vitamin K from the records. This is a minor responsibility-chain omission under RC5, capping the grade at 2 Borderline despite strong high-order performance.
